content: Sister Frances Dominica Ritchie, FRC, is a British nurse who specializes in palliative care. During her childhood, she cared for her younger brother, David Ritchie, who was born with only one lung and was five and a half years younger than her. She frequently visited him at Great Ormond Street Hospital. Later, she attended Cheltenham Ladies' College. Sister Frances chose to pursue palliative care after encountering a two-year-old girl named Helen, who had undergone surgery for a cerebral tumor and was in a comatose state, being cared for at home. To provide relief for Helen's parents, Sister Frances occasionally took the child into her own home. This experience inspired her to establish Helen House in Oxford, the world’s first hospice dedicated to children. She continues to serve as a trustee of Helen House. In January 2007, a documentary series titled The Children of Helen House began airing on BBC2, highlighting the work of the hospice. She later founded Douglas House, a facility designed to provide respite care for individuals aged 16 to 40 with life-shortening conditions. Douglas House, which was opened by Her Majesty The Queen in 2004, is located on the same grounds as Helen House. Both facilities offer respite care, end-of-life care, and family support. Families are welcome to stay with their loved ones if they choose, and support is provided from the time of referral and for as many years after the death of the young person as the family desires. Sister Frances was also a guest on the BBC Radio 4 program Desert Island Discs.
